parts.text: Describe the self report as a research method.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design an alternative way to investigate intergroup categorisation using a self report and
describe how it could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Evaluate this alternative way of studying intergroup categorisation in methodological and
ethical terms.

text: Tajfel carried out a laboratory experiment to investigate intergroup categorisation. An alternative
way to investigate this would be to carry out a self report.

parts.text: What is meant by the ‘developmental approach’?

parts.text: Describe one finding from the study that supports the developmental approach.

Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of the developmental approach using the Nelson
study as an example.

Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Nelson conducted a study to investigate children’s morals using stories.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘psychometric test’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test)
Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder)
Billington et al. (empathising and systemising)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What advantages may psychologists have when they use psychometric tests?

Rosenhan (sane in insane places)
Freud (little Hans)
Mann et al. (lying)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe an application to everyday life for each of these studies.

What problems may psychologists have when they try to make research applicable to
